To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nNOS but eNOS mRNA and proteins are differentially expressed in SHR compared to normotensive controls.

the expression of nOS mRNA and protein are increased in the HPA axis in SHR compared to WKY at prehypertension and hypertension phases, and the expression of eNOS mRNA and iNOS mRNA/protein are unchanged.
neuronal nitric oxide synthases are upregulated in the hypothalamopituitary-adrenocortical axis of hypertensive rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the role of nitric oxide in the hypothalamopituitary-adrenocortical axis of the SHR, a genetic model of hypertension.
the role of nNOS in the HPA axis in SHR during the development of genetic high blood pressure.
the role of nNOS in the HPA axis in SHR during the development of hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nNOS is a major contributor to the pathogenesis of spontaneous hypertension in SHR.
the expression of the three isoforms of nitrate oxide synthase is not altered during the development of genetic (spontaneous) hypertension in rats.
the nNOS protein is increased at prehypetensive and hypertensive ages in the hypothalamu of SHR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of nitrergic system in SHR HPA-axis is differentially regulated at the transcriptional, translational and post-translational levels.
the increased expression of nNOs in the hypothalamopituitary axis may contribute to the pathogenesis of hypertension in SHR.
the nNOS isoforms are differentially regulated in the HPA axis of SHR during the development of hypertension and that this regulation may be important in the development of genetic hypertensions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the differential expression of NOS isoforms in SHR HPA may contribute to the development of hypertension.
there are differential changes in nNOS expression in the HPA axis during the development and progression of hypertension in SHR, which may be important for the pathogenesis of hypertension.
the nNOS isoforms appear to play an important role in the pathogenesis and progression of genetic hypertension.
